title: New Relic POV and Evaluation- Bathroom Planner(Summary)
content:
1 Goal:

To evaluate New Relic APM tool’s monitoring capability and features using Bathroom planner as the subject and parallelly enabling Bathroom planner to establish its requirement of monitoring its operations and web vitals.

Program is driven by IPEX DevOps team lead by joakim.hogart@inter.ikea.com (Solution Architect) supported by

  1. external.sambit.patanaik@inter.ikea.com (Performance Engineer and monitoring specialist)

  2. sigurdur.orn.birgisson@inter.ikea.com (QA lead IPEX)

  3. New Relic Team (rbabu@newrelic.com and sgjessingsepstrup@newrelic.com)

  4. andrea.mazzotti@inter.ikea.com (Platform leader Devops)

  5. lluis.planas@inter.ikea.com (Developer)

  6. arpan.ray1@inter.ikea.com (BP Solution Architect)

2 Top 4 identified monitoring areas for evaluation:

  • Availability

  • Synthetics for performance/response time

  • Hosts/ Infrastructure

  • Browser data

  • Monitoring Logs EC2

4 Findings

Availability:

For Bathroom Planner the availability was defined by two methods. Front end and Back end monitoring. Front end monitoring was designed by a ping test to a monitoring URL, responding with a static response . These front end monitoring are established from various cloud location based on the planners geo presence.

Back end monitoring was designed by a call to the DB with a browser test for a static response again.

Synthetics Monitoring:

For Bathroom planner the synthetic monitoring are designed by scripted browser test to simulate a user planing session using critical user flows or transactions.

Hosts and Infrastructure :

Agents were deployed to pull host usage data. This was done to enable an insight into infra usage in production.

AWS infra, apache servers, lambdas etc are monitored for various performance vitals.

Downstream Browser Data

Browser agent is deployed to capture core webvitals from downstream application usage by the users. This data has the capability to provide the application usage data from an end user perspective, e.g; page views, session traces, Ajax calls, browser type, browser errors, versions etc.

5 Summary

Overall it was a very productive proof of value designed towards enablement of IT operations monitoring for various planners. Bathroom planner was the first to be onboarded and provided with various matrices to evaluate the planners vitals and pulses.

The end result are encouraging but at the same time the usage of production data, user access and license strategy is important for long term sustainability and success.
